derivation: a primitive root (identical with through the idea of narrowness (of orifice));
def: to pour out, i.e. (figuratively) smelt, utter

occurrences.text: Iron is taken out of the earth, and brass is molten out of the stone.
When I washed my steps with butter, and the rock poured me out rivers of oil;
Lord, in trouble have they visited thee, they poured out a prayer when thy chastening was upon them.

source: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890) and Concise Dictionaries (1894), public domain; JSON by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA).
